one_line: Babur, Timurid warlord-king, and Rana Sanga, Rajput ruler of Mewar, facing each other in the decisive battle of Khanwa.

appearance.age_look: Babur appears in his mid-30s, lean and wiry; Rana Sanga appears in his early 40s, tall and broad-shouldered with a veteran’s build.
appearance.face: Babur has an oval face, sharp cheekbones, straight nose, wheatish-light complexion with faint sun-tan, thin arched brows, trimmed moustache and short pointed beard, eyes usually calm and assessing with a slight determined frown; Rana Sanga has a strong square face, deeper brown complexion weathered by sun, broad nose, thick brows, full moustache with neatly curled ends, and a steady, proud gaze, often with a stern, resolute expression.
appearance.hair: Babur’s hair is dark brown, straight and cut short to mid-ear, mostly hidden under a soft, tall, rounded Turkic-style cap made of dark teal cloth with a subtle fur band at the base; Rana Sanga’s hair is black, shoulder-length and tied back in a short knot, partially covered by a domed Rajput helmet of dark steel with a small pointed finial and a narrow nasal bar, wrapped at the base with a dull saffron cloth band.
appearance.costume: Babur wears a quilted, knee-length, front-opening coat (chihraq) of deep red-brown cotton with narrow vertical quilting and thin black piping, over a long-sleeved teal tunic and loose cream-colored trousers tucked into mid-calf leather boots in dark brown; a narrow patterned sash of muted gold and green wraps his waist, with a simple dagger at his left; over his coat he sometimes has a sleeveless, dark indigo over-robe with subtle floral motifs near the hem; Rana Sanga wears a knee-length, mail-and-plate coat over a dark indigo cotton angarkha with crossed front ties, the armour showing small overlapping steel plates and mail rings, with the cloth edges and cuffs in muted maroon; his lower garment is a cream-colored, pleated dhoti-style wrap held with a broad maroon cloth belt, falling to mid-calf, and he wears sturdy brown leather shoes; a light saffron cotton scarf is draped diagonally from his left shoulder under the armour, and he has minimal jewellery—simple iron armlets and a plain ring.
appearance.signature: Babur’s signature prop is a slender, slightly curved Timurid sabre with a plain steel blade, simple cross-guard and dark leather-wrapped hilt held in his right hand, while Rana Sanga’s signature weapon is a long Rajput straight sword (khanda) with a broad double-edged blade and basket hilt, carried in his right hand point-down, its plain iron scabbard slung by a leather belt.

ref_desc: Babur is a lean, mid-30s Timurid in a deep red-brown quilted coat with teal under-tunic, dark teal cap and a curved sabre, while Rana Sanga is a tall Rajput in indigo angarkha, mail-and-plate armour, cream dhoti, saffron scarf, steel helmet and straight khanda, all in deep red-brown, teal, cream, indigo and saffron tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet showing two opposing historical characters standing side by side: Babur, a lean mid-30s Central Asian ruler with an oval, wheatish-light face, sharp cheekbones, trimmed moustache and short pointed beard, wearing a dark teal rounded cap with a subtle fur band, a knee-length deep red-brown vertically quilted coat over a teal long-sleeved tunic and loose cream trousers tucked into dark brown mid-calf leather boots, a narrow muted gold-and-green patterned sash at his waist and holding a slender, slightly curved Timurid sabre with a plain steel blade and dark leather-wrapped hilt; and Rana Sanga, a tall, broad-shouldered Rajput ruler in his early 40s with a square, sun-browned face, full curled moustache and stern gaze, black hair tied back, wearing a domed dark steel Rajput helmet with a small finial and saffron cloth at the base, a visible light saffron scarf draped from his left shoulder, a dark indigo cotton angarkha under a knee-length mail-and-plate coat, a cream pleated dhoti-style wrap to mid-calf held with a maroon belt, sturdy brown leather shoes, simple iron armlets, and carrying a broad straight khanda with basket hilt and plain iron scabbard; keep colours consistent in deep red-brown, dark teal, cream, indigo and saffron, with both figures fully clothed, dignified and ready for battle in historically grounded early 16th-century North Indian and Timurid-inspired attire.
